tier_reason: Upgraded from D: the author's papers and PhD thesis are checked into github.com/bsaleil/bsaleil.github.io/docs and reachable via raw.githubusercontent.com. The thesis (Universite de Montreal, May 2019, Section 6.5.1) compares LC against Gambit v4.9.3 and Chez Scheme v9.5.2 with flags stated (Gambit block/standard-bindings declarations and (not safe); Chez optimize-level 2/3, --program) on an Intel Core i7-7700K, and the harness is public in the repo (tools/benchtimes/run.py with gambit_no_options and chez_no_options, tools/benchtimes/prefix/Gambit.scm and ChezScheme.scm, tools/benchtimes/bench/*.scm); the peer-reviewed VMIL 2018 paper independently reports 1.47x over Gambit on an i7-4870HQ.

corrections.baseline: Gambit Scheme v4.9.3 and Chez Scheme v9.5.2 (mature AOT Scheme compilers, safe and unsafe modes); also Pycket (February 2019 build, Racket tracing JIT on RPython) for total time
corrections.claimed_speedup: PhD thesis (Saleil 2019, Fig. 6.16, execution time excluding GC and compilation time, 38 benchmarks): average execution time relative to LC is Gambit safe 1.38x, Chez safe 1.27x, Gambit unsafe 1.12x, Chez unsafe 1.09x; LC is faster on more than half of the benchmarks; best case fftrad4 with Gambit at 4.03x (safe) / 3.29x (unsafe) and Chez at 5.10x (safe) / 4.60x (unsafe) of LC's time. Against Pycket (Fig. 6.17, including JIT compile time, excluding GC): LC is 0.87x Pycket's time on average (0.80x with f64vectors), faster on 22 of 38, best nucleic 0.13x, worst fft 3.40x. VMIL 2018 paper (Section 6.3, i7-4870HQ, Gambit v4.8.9 cited): LC optimized generated code 1.47x faster than Gambit on average, faster on 26 of 38; 1.35x faster than Pycket on average (22 of 37 significantly faster); 2.25x over LC naive mode. ECOOP 2017 abstract: 'up to 50% faster' refers to interprocedural versus intraprocedural LC; against Gambit unsafe the generated code ranges from 34% faster (browse) to 390% slower (pnpoly). The README fib(40) timing (0.550 s real) has no baseline.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: LC built against the modified Gambit fork (bsaleil/gambit); the Makefile default target compiles LC with gsc -prelude "(declare (not safe))" and config-release.scm (README shows make debug); benchmark runs use --max-versions 5 with interprocedural specialization, tagging and eager flonum unboxing. Gambit v4.9.3: gsc -:m512000 -exe with prefix (declare (standard-bindings) (extended-bindings) (block)), plus (not safe) for unsafe mode. Chez Scheme 9.5.2 single-threaded build: compile-program, optimize-level 2 (safe) or 3 (unsafe), run with scheme --program. The optimize-level and (not safe) settings are stated in the thesis text, not in the committed harness.
corrections.hardware: Thesis: Intel Core i7-7700K 4.20 GHz, 16 GB DDR4, GNU/Linux (otherwise unused machine). VMIL 2018 and ECOOP 2017: Intel Core i7-4870HQ, 16 GB DDR3, GNU/Linux; 10 runs per benchmark, min and max dropped, mean of the remaining 8.
corrections.workload: JIT compiler for Scheme on Linux x86-64 using lazy basic-block versioning with interprocedural code specialization (entry and return point tables). Experiments use 38 classic Scheme benchmarks taken from Gambit with Gambit's iteration counts (ack, boyer, browse, compiler, conform, cpstak, deriv, earley, fft, fftrad4, fib, fibfp, mbrot, nbody, nqueens, nucleic, peval, pnpoly, simplex, sum, sumfp, tak, takl and others), driven by tools/benchtimes/run.py; the Gambit and Chez comparison times generated code only (GC and compile time excluded), the Pycket comparison includes JIT compile time.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 33 stars, 1 fork; ECOOP 2017 (artifact-evaluated, DARTS 3.2.14), VMIL 2018, SFPW 2014 and SFPW 2015 papers, and Baptiste Saleil's 2019 Universite de Montreal PhD thesis
corrections.caveats: Research JIT, last commit 2019-05-11, abandoned; x86-64 Linux only and needs the author's modified Gambit fork. The averages are modest and mode-dependent: LC skips vector bounds checks, stack-overflow checks and interrupt polling (the thesis cites about 15% polling overhead for Gambit), so the safe-mode leads (1.38x Gambit, 1.27x Chez) partly compare unequal safety, and in unsafe mode the lead shrinks to 1.12x and 1.09x with LC losing on a large minority of benchmarks; the Gambit and Chez times exclude GC and compilation time. VMIL 2018 lists missing features (no first-class continuations, limited eval). The repo commits no timing results; the numbers live in the papers and thesis (PDFs in github.com/bsaleil/bsaleil.github.io/docs; the dagstuhl and schemeworkshop.org copies were EGRESS_BLOCKED). The harness hard-codes the author's /home/bapt paths, has every system except LC5 commented out, and does not set Chez's optimize-level or Gambit's (not safe) mode, which only the thesis states. The ECOOP 2017 'up to 50% faster' figure is LC interprocedural versus LC intraprocedural, not versus Gambit or Chez.

notes: Upgrade D to A with verdict confirm: the papers the search agent could not reach are in the author's bsaleil.github.io repo, and the thesis gives Gambit v4.9.3 and Chez 9.5.2 comparisons with flags and CPU, backed by the public tools/benchtimes harness and the peer-reviewed VMIL 2018 result (1.47x over Gambit). Shortcomings to record: modest averages (1.12x/1.09x in unsafe mode), safety-check asymmetry in safe mode, GC and compile time excluded, harness with hard-coded paths and modes set outside it, abandoned since 2019. Baselines gambit/gambit and cisco/chezscheme are already in the catalog.

tier_reason: README Octane 2.0 table compares goant (interpreter and baseline JIT) against goja in one sitting, with the harness public (cmd/goant-bench/main.go, bench/suites/fetch.sh pinning chromium/octane 570ad1cc, bench/gojarun and bench/ottorun runner modules), Go 1.26.3 with CGO_ENABLED=0, pinned goja version and an Azure D8s_v5 Xeon Platinum 8370C stated; the third-party ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark table independently shows goant ahead of goja.

corrections.claimed_speedup: README Octane table, goant+JIT versus goja versus QuickJS: Richards 1374 / 218 / 836, DeltaBlue 929 / 271 / 818, Crypto 2320 / 127 / 1099, RayTrace 557 / 304 / 995, EarleyBoyer 822 / 540 / 1598, RegExp 276 / 212 / 268, Splay 2320 / 2138 / 3426, NavierStokes 6012 / 202 / 1971. Interpreter-only goant (JIT off): 227, 258, 257, 431, 536, 238, 1874, 467, so it beats goja on 5 of 8 (about 1.26x geometric mean, derived from page data) and beats QuickJS on none. goant+JIT beats goja on 8 of 8 (about 3.8x geometric mean, derived from page data; up to 29.8x on NavierStokes, derived from page data) and QuickJS on 5 of 8 (about 1.1x geometric mean, derived from page data). README: JIT is worth 3.1x over all fifteen Octane workloads. Node on the same machine scores 33,300 on Richards against goant+JIT 1374, so V8 is one to two orders of magnitude ahead. Third-party ahaoboy/js-engine-benchmark README (run 10/5/2026, goant v0.2.1.9a81153) total score on ubuntu: goant 981, goja 264, Paserati 401, QuickJS 2026.06.04 1217, quickjs-ng 0.17.0 647, ant 2186, V8 48107, Node 40333; macos-arm64: goant 1363, goja 436, QuickJS 1761; windows: goant 964, goja 218, QuickJS 1067.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 7 stars, 0 forks, 1,326 commits; embedded in Robomotion RPA robots (README)
corrections.caveats: goant is a C-to-Go port of the Silver engine from theMackabu/ant (README Credits: 'the architecture, the opcode set and the conformance bar are all its'), which is already in the catalog as https://github.com/themackabu/ant; ant itself scores 2186 against goant's 981 on the ahaoboy ubuntu table and is 1.1x to 3.5x faster than the goant interpreter on six of seven README rows. goant adds its own baseline JIT. Project is first-party and young (7 stars; v0.2.0 and v0.2.1 release-note commits on 2026-08-19/20, but the README says there is no tagged release yet, so go get pins a commit). Only eight of fifteen Octane workloads are tabulated against the competitors; the all-fifteen 3.1x JIT figure is from an earlier run on an identically specified instance, and the otto column was added later on the same machine. Best of two runs; Splay is noisy. The headline 3.8x over goja compares a baseline JIT with an interpreter; interpreter against interpreter the lead is about 1.26x and goja wins DeltaBlue, EarleyBoyer and Splay. QuickJS is the 2021-03-27 build with no build flags stated, and QuickJS wins RayTrace, EarleyBoyer and Splay even against goant+JIT; in the third-party ahaoboy suite goant scores below QuickJS 2026.06.04 on all three OSes while beating goja, Paserati and quickjs-ng; the ahaoboy README does not state the runner CPU. The JIT is off by default when embedded; it has differential fuzzing but no darwin/amd64 stress test.

notes: All README Octane, environment and ahaoboy numbers match; derived ratios recomputed (1.26x, 3.83x, 1.12x, 29.8x). Possible duplicate: goant is a Go port of the already-listed themackabu/ant (go-quickjs precedent folded a Go port of quickjs-ng as duplicate), though it adds its own baseline JIT and is measured against goja, a different baseline. Shortcomings to record: JIT vs interpreter headline, interpreter-only lead only 1.26x, loses to QuickJS and to ant, 2021 QuickJS build, young first-party project.
